title: Speaking of the majlis…: building on a point
goal: In the university library, plan your group's seminar talk with your classmate Khalfān: do you need Arabic in Dubai? Build on each of his points
tip: Take up his point before you add yours: mithil ma gilt… 'as you said…', ana wiyyāk fi han-nugṭa 'I'm with you on that'. Then add your own angle: min hādhi z-zāwiya… And ʿala ṭāri + a word he just used picks it up: ʿala ṭāri l-majālis… 'speaking of majlises…'.
grammar: building on a point (mithil ma gilt, min hādhi z-zāwiya, ʿala ṭāri)
dialogue: A
يلا، خلنا نسوي خطة العرض. موضوعنا: تحتاج العربي في دبي، ولّا يكفيك الإنقليزي؟
yalla, khallna nsawwi khiṭṭat il-ʿarẓ. mawẓūʿna: tiḥtāj il-ʿarabi fi Dbayy, walla ykaffīk il-inglīzi?
Right, let's make a plan for the talk. Our topic: do you need Arabic in Dubai, or is English enough?
B
زين. شو أول نقطة عندك؟
zēn. shu awwal nugṭa ʿindak?
OK. What's your first point?
A
الشغل. في أغلب الشركات، الشغل كله بالإنقليزي
ish-shughul. fi aghlab ish-sharikāt, ish-shughul killah bil-inglīzi
Work. In most companies, all the work's in English.
B
مثل ما قلت، الشغل بالإنقليزي، وأنا وياك في هالنقطة
mithil ma gilt, ish-shughul bil-inglīzi, w ana wiyyāk fi han-nugṭa
As you said, work's in English, and I'm with you on that point.
A
بس؟ يعني نقول للناس العربي ما له داعي؟
bas? yaʿni ngūl lin-nās il-ʿarabi ma lah dāʿi?
Is that it? So we tell people there's no point in Arabic?
B
لا، ما تقدر تتجاهل الناس. من هذي الزاوية، العربي مرتبط بالثقة
la, ma tigdar titjāhal in-nās. min hādhi z-zāwiya, il-ʿarabi mirtabiṭ bith-thiga
No, you can't leave people out. From that angle, Arabic is tied up with trust.
A
حلو! والمجالس؟ ما تقدر تسولف فيها بالإنقليزي
ḥilu! w il-majālis? ma tigdar tsōlif fīha bil-inglīzi
Nice! And majlises? You can't chat in them in English.
B
على طاري المجالس، بو راشد يقول الأمثال ما لها ترجمة
ʿala ṭāri l-majālis, Bū Rāshid ygūl il-amthāl ma lha tarjama
Speaking of majlises, Bū Rāshid says proverbs don't translate.
A
ممتاز، نحن على نفس الموجة! هذي نقطتنا الثالثة. بس ترا ما خلصت كلامي!
mumtāz, niḥin ʿala nafs il-mōja! hādhi nugṭatna th-thālitha. bas tara ma khallaṣt kalāmi!
Great, we're on the same wavelength! That's our third point. But I hadn't finished, you know!
B
سوري، كمل كلامك. وأنا أكتب الخطة، بلا تكرار
sōri, kammil kalāmak. w ana aktib il-khiṭṭa, bala tikrār
Sorry, go on. And I'll write up the plan, with nothing said twice.
items: speaking of, talking of (picking up what was just said)
you ignore, you leave out (to a man)
from that angle, looking at it that way
tied up with, linked to (a masculine thing)
a feminine thing: mirtabṭa b- (مرتبطة ب)

title: Order, everyone! Chairing a meeting
goal: At the office, Bū Saʿīd has asked you to chair the weekly team meeting; take Maryam's report, stop an argument, and keep to time
tip: A chair opens the floor (minu yabi yiṭraḥ shay? 'does anyone want to raise anything?'), sets the order (il-awlawiyya lit-tagrīr 'the report comes first', nitnāgash fīh ākhir shay 'we'll discuss it last') and calms things down: shwayy hudūʼ, ana muḥāyid, ma nabi jidāl.
grammar: chairing a meeting (yiṭraḥ, il-awlawiyya, nitnāgash fīh, hudūʼ)
dialogue: A
صباح الخير. بو سعيد يقول انت بتدير الاجتماع اليوم؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr. Bū Saʿīd ygūl inta bitdīr il-ijtimāʿ il-yōm?
Good morning. Bū Saʿīd says you're chairing the meeting today?
B
صباح النور. هيه. منو يبي يطرح شي قبل لا نبدا؟
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. hē. minu yabi yiṭraḥ shay gabil la nibda?
Good morning. Yes. Does anyone want to raise anything before we start?
A
أنا. السيستم اليديد فيه مشكلة، والكل يشتكي
ana. is-sistim il-yidīd fīh mushkila, w il-kill yishtiki
Me. The new system has a problem, and everyone's complaining.
B
زين، نتناقش فيه آخر شي. الأولوية للتقرير: وين وصلتي فيه؟
zēn, nitnāgash fīh ākhir shay. il-awlawiyya lit-tagrīr: wēn wiṣalti fīh?
OK, we'll discuss it last. The report comes first: how far have you got with it?
A
خلصته، وطرشته للعميل الصبح
khallaṣtah, w ṭarrashtah lil-ʿamīl iṣ-ṣubḥ
I've finished it, and I sent it to the client this morning.
B
ممتاز. الموضوع الثاني: حفلة آخر السنة. وين تبون تسوونها؟
mumtāz. il-mawẓūʿ ith-thāni: ḥaflat ākhir is-sana. wēn tabūn tsawwūnha?
Great. Next item: the end-of-year party. Where do you all want to have it?
A
نص الفريق يبي مطعم، والنص الثاني يبي البر. وصار بينهم جدال!
nuṣṣ il-farīg yabi maṭʿam, w in-nuṣṣ ith-thāni yabi l-barr. w ṣār bēnhum jidāl!
Half the team want a restaurant, and the other half want the desert. And they've started arguing!
B
شوي هدوء يا جماعة! أنا محايد، وما نبي جدال
shwayy hudūʼ yā jamāʿa! ana muḥāyid, w ma nabi jidāl
A bit of quiet, everyone! I'm not taking sides, and we don't want an argument.
A
معك حق. بس الوقت ما يكفي نقرر اليوم
maʿak ḥagg. bas il-wagt ma ykaffi ngarrir il-yōm
You're right. But there isn't enough time to decide today.
B
خلاص، نأجلها للاجتماع الياي. والحين، السيستم
khalāṣ, nʼajjilha lil-ijtimāʿ il-yāy. w il-ḥīn, is-sistim
Fine, we'll put it off to the next meeting. And now, the system.
items: (to) raise something, (to) bring something up (in a meeting)
we('ll) discuss it (m.), we('ll) talk it over
a feminine thing: nitnāgash fīha (نتناقش فيها)
a bit of quiet, please: shwayy hudūʼ

title: In two lines, sir: summarising
goal: At the office, Bū Saʿīd missed the team meeting you chaired; give him the main points in short, respectfully, and the one problem still open
tip: A senior wants the headline first. Answer shu abraz shay? with the short version (fi saṭrēn 'in a couple of lines'), then what's open (fīh khalal 'there's a fault'), then the heart of it: il-jawhar inn… 'the heart of it is that…'. Keep ṭāl ʿumrak in every second line or so.
grammar: summarising for a senior (abraz shay, fi saṭrēn, il-jawhar inn…)
dialogue: A
هلا سالم. ما قدرت أحضر الاجتماع. شو أبرز شي صار؟
hala Sālim. ma gidart aḥẓar il-ijtimāʿ. shu abraz shay ṣār?
Hello, Sālim. I couldn't make the meeting. What was the main thing that happened?
B
هلا بك، طال عمرك. في سطرين: التقرير وصل للعميل، والباقي تفاصيل
hala bik, ṭāl ʿumrak. fi saṭrēn: it-tagrīr wiṣal lil-ʿamīl, w il-bāgi tafāṣīl
Hello, sir. In a couple of lines: the report's with the client, and the rest is detail.
A
زين. وفي عوايق في السيستم اليديد؟ سمعت الكل يشتكي
zēn. w fī ʿawāyig fi s-sistim il-yidīd? simaʿt il-kill yishtiki
Good. And are there any snags with the new system? I heard everyone's complaining.
B
هيه، فيه خلل. اتفقنا على خطة: مريم تكلم الشركة، وأنا أتابع
hē, fīh khalal. ittafagna ʿala khiṭṭa: Maryam tkallim ish-sharika, w ana atābiʿ
Yes, there's a fault. We agreed on a plan: Maryam calls the company, and I follow it up.
A
والحفلة؟ سمعت إن الشباب مختلفين
w il-ḥafla? simaʿt inn ish-shabāb mikhtalfīn
And the party? I heard the lads can't agree.
B
صح، وأجلناها للاجتماع الياي، طال عمرك
ṣaḥḥ, w ajjalnāha lil-ijtimāʿ il-yāy, ṭāl ʿumrak
Right, and we've put it off to the next meeting, sir.
A
يعني شو الجوهر؟
yaʿni shu l-jawhar?
So what's the heart of it?
B
الجوهر إن الشغل ماشي، بس الخلل لازم ينحل
il-jawhar inn ish-shughul māshi, bas il-khalal lāzim yinḥall
The heart of it is that the work's on track, but the fault has to be sorted out.
A
ما شاء الله، ملخص مرتب. يعطيك العافية
mā shāʼ allāh, mulakhkhaṣ mrattab. yaʿṭīk il-ʿāfya
Mā shāʼ allāh, a tidy summary. Thanks for your hard work.
B
الله يعافيك. وأنا متفائل، طال عمرك
allāh yʿāfīk. w ana mitfāʼil, ṭāl ʿumrak
Thank you. And I'm optimistic, sir.
items: the main thing, the biggest thing (that happened)
in a couple of lines, in short
there's a fault, something's wrong (with it)
the heart of it, the core (of the matter)

title: Prove it! A debate at university
goal: In a seminar debate, your classmate Sulṭān argues that English is enough to live in Dubai; take him on point by point
tip: Answer the argument, not the man. Concede what's true first (ma ankir inn… 'I don't deny that…'), then name the weak spot (hādhi ḥujja nāgṣa, hādha tanāquẓ), and when he calls you ʿāṭifi 'emotional', answer with your own experience.
grammar: debating (ma ankir inn, ḥujja, tanāquẓ, ma tigdar tinfi)
dialogue: A
الإنقليزي لغة العالم. وفي دبي تقدر تعيش سنين بدون ولا كلمة عربي
il-inglīzi lughat il-ʿālam. w fi Dbayy tigdar tiʿīsh snīn bidūn wala kilma ʿarabi
English is the world's language. And in Dubai you can live for years without a single word of Arabic.
B
ما أنكر إن الإنقليزي مهم، بس عطني دليل
ma ankir inn il-inglīzi muhimm, bas ʿaṭni dalīl
I don't deny that English matters, but give me proof.
A
عندي إحصائيات: أغلب الموظفين في الشركات يشتغلون بالإنقليزي
ʿindi iḥṣāʼiyyāt: aghlab il-muwaẓẓafīn fi sh-sharikāt yishtaghlūn bil-inglīzi
I've got statistics: most employees in companies work in English.
B
ممكن، بس الشغل مب كل الحياة. هذي حجة ناقصة
mumkin, bas ish-shughul mub kill il-ḥayā. hādhi ḥujja nāgṣa
Maybe, but work isn't the whole of life. That argument's incomplete.
A
ربعي الأجانب كلهم مرتاحين، وما يتكلمون عربي
rabʿi l-ajānib killhum mirtāḥīn, w ma yitkallamūn ʿarabi
My foreign friends are all happy, and they don't speak Arabic.
B
بس أمس قلت إنهم ما يعرفون حد هني. هذا تناقض!
bas ams gilt innahum ma yaʿarfūn ḥad hni. hādha tanāquẓ!
But yesterday you said they don't know anyone here. That's a contradiction!
A
هذا كلام عاطفي، مب أرقام
hādha kalām ʿāṭifi, mub argām
That's emotional talk, not figures.
B
مب عاطفي، وما تقدر تنفي: لما تكلمت عربي، الناس فتحوا لي مجالسهم
mub ʿāṭifi, w ma tigdar tinfi: lamma tkallamt ʿarabi, in-nās fitḥaw-li majālis-hum
It's not emotional, and you can't deny it: when I spoke Arabic, people opened their majlises to me.
A
صح، معك حق في هذي. بس انت حالة خاصة
ṣaḥḥ, maʿak ḥagg fi hādhi. bas inta ḥāla khāṣṣa
True, you're right on that one. But you're a special case.
B
يمكن. بس حجتك تحتاج دليل، وأنا عندي تجربة
yimkin. bas ḥujjatak tiḥtāj dalīl, w ana ʿindi tajruba
Maybe. But your argument needs proof, and I've got experience.
items: I don't deny that, I won't deny that
an argument, a case (in a debate)
to a woman: tinfīn (تنفين); you can't deny it: ma tigdar tinfi
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search a tutoring site for «Emirati Arabic tutor»), hold a 10-minute debate: they say English is enough in Dubai; you argue for Arabic. Concede once (ma ankir inn…), ask for proof (ʿaṭni dalīl) and name a weak point (ḥujja nāgṣa, tanāquẓ). Then sum up your side in one minute as if to Bū Saʿīd (ṭāl ʿumrak, fi saṭrēn).

title: Don't back out now! Debating with Fahad
goal: On a video call from Kuwait, Fahad hears you won the seminar debate and challenges you: Kuwaiti or Emirati? Hold your ground with a friend
tip: With a friend the same moves get playful. Tease back instead of proving: la titfalsaf ʿalay 'don't lecture me', la tishmit 'don't gloat', and la tistafizzni 'don't wind me up'. When he asks tabi tinsiḥib? 'want to back out?', refuse and offer a draw.
grammar: debating with a friend (la tishmit, la tistafizzni, tinsiḥib)
dialogue: A
سمعت إنك غلبت سلطان! تبي مباراة ثانية؟ الكويتي أحلى من الإماراتي!
simaʿt innak ghalabt Sulṭān! tabi mubārā thānya? il-kwēti aḥla min il-imārāti!
I heard you beat Sulṭān! Want another match? Kuwaiti's nicer than Emirati!
B
مباراة حلوة. بس لا تتفلسف علي!
mubārā ḥilwa. bas la titfalsaf ʿalay!
Good match. But don't go lecturing me!
A
أنا؟ ما أتفلسف. الكويتي عال العال، وكل الخليج يفهمه
ana? ma atfalsaf. il-kwēti ʿāl il-ʿāl, w kill il-khalīj yifhamah
Me? I'm not lecturing. Kuwaiti's top-notch, and the whole Gulf understands it.
B
لا تستفزني! الإماراتي بعد الكل يفهمه
la tistafizzni! il-imārāti baʿad il-kill yifhamah
Don't wind me up! Everyone understands Emirati too.
A
إيه، بس شو هالعنجهية؟ لا تصير مغرور لأنك غلبت سلطان!
ēh, bas shu hal-ʿanjahiyya? la tṣīr maghrūr lannak ghalabt Sulṭān!
Yeah, but what's this arrogance? Don't get big-headed because you beat Sulṭān!
B
مب مغرور! وانت لا تشمت إذا غلبتك
mub maghrūr! w inta la tishmit idha ghalabtak
I'm not big-headed! And don't you gloat if I beat you.
A
زين، تبي تنسحب؟
zēn, tabi tinsiḥib?
OK, do you want to back out?
B
لا أبد! حتى لو كلامك صح، الإماراتي اللي أسمعه كل يوم
la abad! ḥatta lō kalāmak ṣaḥḥ, il-imārāti illi asmaʿah kill yōm
No way! Even if you're right, Emirati is what I hear every day.
A
ماشي، تعادلنا. بس لا تعايرني إذا خسرت المباراة الياية!
māshi, tʿādalna. bas la tʿāyirni idha khisirt il-mubārā l-yāya!
Fine, it's a draw. But don't rub it in if I lose the next match!
B
ماشي، والغدا على حسابي!
māshi, w il-ghada ʿala ḥsābi!
Deal, and lunch is on me!
items: to a woman: la tishmitīn (لا تشمتين)
you back out, you pull out (to a man)
don't wind me up, don't provoke me (to a man)
to a woman: la tistafizzīni (لا تستفزيني)
don't rub it in, don't taunt me (with it) (to a man)
to a woman: la tʿāyrīni (لا تعايريني)

title: Three points, five minutes: the rehearsal
goal: In the university library, rehearse your seminar talk in front of your classmate Mājid, and take his advice on nerves, voice and the audience
tip: Say how nerves hit you, in the past or as a habit: irtabakt 'I got flustered', aḥiss inni atlaʿtham 'I feel I'm stammering', īdi tirtiʿish 'my hand's shaking'. Mājid answers with commands: khudh nafas ʿamīg, irfaʿ ṣōtak.
grammar: recycle: past and present for nerves (irtabakt, atlaʿtham, tirtiʿish); commands for advice
dialogue: A
يلا، ابدا العرض. تخيل إنك على المسرح والجمهور يطالعك
yalla, ibda l-ʿarẓ. tkhayyal innak ʿala l-masraḥ w il-jumhūr yṭālʿak
Go on, start the talk. Imagine you're on the stage and the audience is watching you.
B
بسم الله. عندي ثلاث نقاط… لا، ارتبكت! هذا كابوس!
bismillāh. ʿindi thalāth nigāṭ… la, irtabakt! hādha kābūs!
In God's name. I've got three points… no, I've lost my nerve! This is a nightmare!
A
عادي، كل واحد يرتبك أول مرة. خذ نفس عميق
ʿādi, kill wāḥid yirtibik awwal marra. khudh nafas ʿamīg
That's normal; everyone gets flustered the first time. Take a deep breath.
B
أحس إني أتلعثم، وإيدي ترتعش
aḥiss inni atlaʿtham, w īdi tirtiʿish
I feel I'm stammering, and my hand's shaking.
A
ما بان عليك. بس صوتك واطي، ارفعه شوي
ma bān ʿalēk. bas ṣōtak wāṭi, irfaʿah shwayy
It didn't show. But your voice is too low; raise it a bit.
B
زين. وأطالع الورقة ولّا الجمهور؟
zēn. w aṭāliʿ il-waraga walla l-jumhūr?
OK. And do I look at my notes or at the audience?
A
الجمهور! الورقة بس للنقاط، والباقي من راسك
il-jumhūr! il-waraga bas lin-nigāṭ, w il-bāgi min rāsak
The audience! The notes are just for the points; the rest comes from your head.
B
فكرة حلوة. وأبدا بسؤال للجمهور، صح؟
fikra ḥilwa. w abda b-suʼāl lil-jumhūr, ṣaḥḥ?
Good idea. And I start with a question for the audience, right?
A
بالضبط. وكل يوم تمرين، لين يوم الأربعا
biẓ-ẓabṭ. w kill yōm tamrīn, lēn yōm il-arbaʿa
Exactly. And practise every day, till Wednesday.
B
إن شاء الله. ويوم الأربعا ما بتلعثم!
in shāʼ allāh. w yōm il-arbaʿa ma batlaʿtham!
God willing. And on Wednesday I won't stammer!
items: I stammer, I stumble over my words
my hand's shaking, my hand's trembling
take a deep breath (to a man): khudh nafas ʿamīg

title: The goat can't see its tail: proverbs II
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Rāshid there, ask him for Emirati proverbs for the last point of your talk, and work out what each one means
tip: Proverbs are for recognising: let Bū Rāshid say them. Your part is to ask for one and check the meaning: abi amthāl shaʿbiyya, then yaʿni l-maghza inn…? 'so the moral is that…?'. A proverb's verb stays as it is: min kabbar il-lugma ghaṣṣ, not ykabbir.
grammar: recycle: illi 'whoever' and yaʿni … inn to check a meaning; proverbs for recognition
dialogue: A
سمعت إن عرضك عن العربي في دبي. كيف أقدر أساعدك يا ولدي؟
simaʿt inn ʿarẓak ʿan il-ʿarabi fi Dbayy. chēf agdar asāʿdak yā wildi?
I hear your talk's about Arabic in Dubai. How can I help you, son?
B
أبي أمثال شعبية يا عمي، للنقطة الأخيرة
abi amthāl shaʿbiyya yā ʿammi, lin-nugṭa l-akhīra
I'd like some folk proverbs, uncle, for the last point.
A
أول شي لك انت: خير الكلام ما قل ودل. لا تطول عليهم!
awwal shay lak inta: khēr il-kalām ma gall w dall. la tṭawwil ʿalēhum!
First, one for you: the best words are few and to the point. Don't drag it out for them!
B
صدقت والله! وشي للي يقولون الإنقليزي يكفي؟
ṣidagt wallāh! w shay lilli ygūlūn il-inglīzi ykaffi?
Too true! And something for people who say English is enough?
A
اللي ما يعرفك ما يثمنك. واللي ما يكلمك بلهجتك، ما يعرفك صج
illi ma yaʿarfak ma ythammnak. w illi ma ykallmak b-lahjatak, ma yaʿarfak ṣij
Whoever doesn't know you can't value you. And whoever doesn't talk to you in your own dialect doesn't really know you.
B
يعني المغزى إن اللغة تقرب الناس؟
yaʿni l-maghza inn il-lugha tgarrib in-nās?
So the moral is that language brings people closer?
A
بالضبط. وخلفان؟ راشد يقول إنه يشوف غلط الكل
biẓ-ẓabṭ. w Khalfān? Rāshid ygūl innah yshūf ghalaṭ il-kill
Exactly. And Khalfān? Rāshid says he sees everyone's mistakes.
B
هيه، غلط الكل، إلا غلطه هو!
hē, ghalaṭ il-kill, illa ghalaṭah huwa!
Yes, everyone's mistakes except his own!
A
العنز ما تشوف ذيلها! بس لا تحط عشرين مثل في العرض: من كبر اللقمة غص
il-ʿanz ma tshūf dhēlha! bas la tḥuṭṭ ʿishrīn mathal fi l-ʿarẓ: min kabbar il-lugma ghaṣṣ
The goat can't see its own tail! But don't put twenty proverbs in the talk: whoever takes too big a mouthful chokes.
B
ما بنسى المغزى يا عمي. بحط ثلاثة بس!
ma bansa l-maghza yā ʿammi. baḥuṭṭ thalātha bas!
I won't forget the moral, uncle. I'll only put in three!
items: khēr il-kalām ma gall w dall
the best words are few and to the point (a proverb)
whoever doesn't know you can't value you (a proverb)
(recognise) someone who hasn't dealt with you won't give you your due
the goat can't see its own tail (a proverb)
(recognise) said of someone who sees other people's faults but not their own
whoever takes too big a mouthful chokes (a proverb)
(recognise) said of someone who grabs more than his share
the moral, the point (of a story or a proverb)
culture: Emirati proverbs (amthāl) belong to Bedouin and town life alike, and older people use them to say a lot in a few words. Some have reached English only in transliteration, such as ad-dunya gāfla, ḥad yrūḥ w ḥad yidwi, 'life is a caravan: one leaves, one arrives', said of the turn of the generations.

title: C1 exit: Do you need Arabic in Dubai?
goal: C1 exit: at the university seminar, give your five-minute talk on Arabic in Dubai, and answer your classmate Khalfān, who argues the other side
tip: Review, now in one talk: announce your points, build on the other side (mithil ma gāl Khalfān…), pick up a word (ʿala ṭāri…), answer an objection (khallni arudd), and close with the upshot. New: yaʼaththir ʿala…, jisr, il-mīza, tsidd il-fajwa.
grammar: C1 exit: extended presentation (building on a point, debating, summarising)
dialogue: A
يلا يا سالم، تفضل. عندك خمس دقايق بالكثير
yalla yā Sālim, tfaẓẓal. ʿindak khams dagāyig bil-kathīr
Go on, Sālim, the floor's yours. You've got five minutes at most.
B
بسم الله. سؤالنا: تحتاج العربي في دبي؟ عندي ثلاث نقاط
bismillāh. suʼālna: tiḥtāj il-ʿarabi fi Dbayy? ʿindi thalāth nigāṭ
In God's name. Our question: do you need Arabic in Dubai? I've got three points.
A
أول نقطة الشغل، وهو كله بالإنقليزي، صح؟
awwal nugṭa sh-shughul, w huwa killah bil-inglīzi, ṣaḥḥ?
The first point is work, and that's all in English, right?
B
مثل ما قال خلفان، الشغل بالإنقليزي. بس العربي يأثر على الثقة
mithil ma gāl Khalfān, ish-shughul bil-inglīzi. bas il-ʿarabi yaʼaththir ʿala th-thiga
As Khalfān said, work's in English. But Arabic affects trust.
A
والناس؟ كلهم يتكلمون إنقليزي
w in-nās? killhum yitkallamūn inglīzi
And people? They all speak English.
B
على طاري الناس، من تجربتي، العربي جسر بيني وبينهم
ʿala ṭāri n-nās, min tajrubti, il-ʿarabi jisr bēni w bēnhum
Speaking of people, from my experience, Arabic is a bridge between me and them.
A
بس انت حالة خاصة! ومع العولمة، الفجوة بين اللغتين كل يوم تكبر
bas inta ḥāla khāṣṣa! w maʿa l-ʿawlama, il-fajwa bēn il-lughtēn kill yōm tikbar
But you're a special case! And with globalisation, the gap between the two languages grows every day.
B
خلني أرد. هذي الميزة: مب لازم تتعلم كل شي، كلمتين باللهجة تسد الفجوة
khallni arudd. hādhi l-mīza: mub lāzim titʿallam kill shay; kilmitēn bil-lahja tsidd il-fajwa
Let me answer that. That's the good thing: you don't have to learn everything; a couple of words of dialect close the gap.
A
زين، والنقطة الثالثة؟
zēn, w in-nugṭa th-thālitha?
OK, and the third point?
B
اللغة نفسها: أمثالها ما لها ترجمة. والخلاصة: الإنقليزي يفتح الباب، والعربي يفتح المجلس
il-lugha nafsha: amthālha ma lha tarjama. w il-khulāṣa: il-inglīzi yiftaḥ il-bāb, w il-ʿarabi yiftaḥ il-majlis
The language itself: its proverbs don't translate. And the upshot: English opens the door, and Arabic opens the majlis.
items: a feminine thing: taʼaththir ʿala (تأثر على)
a masculine thing: ysidd (يسد); close the gap: tsidd il-fajwa
the advantage, the good thing (about it)

title: C1 exit: one talk, three voices
goal: C1 exit: in Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf on a video call from abroad, give your talk as at university, as to your manager and as majlis talk
tip: One message, three registers: formal (yisharrifni atkallam ʿan…, il-ʿādāt w it-taqālīd), office (ṭāl ʿumrak, fi saṭrēn), majlis (wallāh, short and warm). Then close the way the majlis closes: a blessing and its reply, and thanks to the people who stood by you (intu sanadi).
grammar: C1 exit: register shifting (formal, office, majlis) on one topic
dialogue: A
حياكم الله! وسيف ويانا من الغربة على الفيديو. سالم صار نجم الجامعة!
ḥayyākum allāh! w Sēf wiyyāna min il-ghurba ʿala l-fīdyo. Sālim ṣār najim il-jāmʿa!
Welcome! And Sēf's with us from abroad on video. Sālim's become the star of the university!
B
الله يحييك يا عمي. عرض صغير، مب أكثر
allāh yḥayyīk yā ʿammi. ʿarẓ ṣghayyir, mub akthar
Thank you, uncle. A little talk, nothing more.
A
لا تتواضع! قوله لعمي مثل ما قلته في الجامعة
la titwāẓaʿ! gūlah l-ʿammi mithil ma giltah fi l-jāmʿa
Don't be modest! Say it for my uncle the way you said it at the university.
B
يشرفني أتكلم عن العربي، لأنه جزء من العادات والتقاليد والحياة في دبي
yisharrifni atkallam ʿan il-ʿarabi, lannah juzʼ min il-ʿādāt w it-taqālīd w il-ḥayā fi Dbayy
It's my honour to speak about Arabic, because it's part of the customs, the traditions and the life of Dubai. (formal)
A
ما شاء الله، كنك في الإذاعة! وكيف تقولها لمديرك؟
mā shāʼ allāh, chinnak fi l-idhāʿa! w chēf tgūlha l-mudīrak?
Mā shāʼ allāh, it's as if you're on the radio! And how would you say it to your manager?
B
طال عمرك، في سطرين: العربي يساعدنا وايد ويا العملاء
ṭāl ʿumrak, fi saṭrēn: il-ʿarabi ysāʿidna wāyid wiyya l-ʿumala
Sir, in a couple of lines: Arabic helps us a great deal with clients. (respectful)
A
والحين مثل ما نسولف هني، يا ريّال! وكيف اندمجت ويانا؟
w il-ḥīn mithil ma nsōlif hni, yā rayyāl! w chēf indamajt wiyyāna?
And now the way we talk here, mate! And how did you fit in with us so well?
B
والله، الإنقليزي يفتح لك الباب، بس العربي يفتح لك المجلس! وهاللمة سوت الباقي
wallāh, il-inglīzi yiftaḥ-lak il-bāb, bas il-ʿarabi yiftaḥ-lak il-majlis! w hal-lamma sawwat il-bāgi
Honestly, English opens the door for you, but Arabic opens the majlis! And gatherings like this one did the rest.
A
هذا الكلام! مجلسنا عريق، وانت صرت واحد منا وعزوة لنا. الله يحفظك
hādha l-kalām! majlisna ʿarīg, w inta ṣirt wāḥid minna w ʿizwa lana. allāh yiḥfaẓak
Now that's talking! Ours is an old majlis, and you've become one of us, someone we're proud of. God keep you.
B
الله يحفظك يا عمي. انتو سندي، ولولاكم جان ما تعلمت ولا كلمة!
allāh yiḥfaẓak yā ʿammi. intu sanadi, w lōlākum chān ma tʿallamt wala kilma!
God keep you, uncle. You've all been my support, and if it weren't for you I wouldn't have learnt a single word!
items: you fitted in, you settled in (to a man); I fitted in
this gathering, a get-together like this (of family and friends)
old and respected, long-established (a family, a majlis)
someone the family is proud of and can lean on
my support, the people I lean on
task: This week: pick a topic you care about and record it three times, 2 minutes each: as a short formal talk (yisharrifni atkallam ʿan…), as a summary for a manager (ṭāl ʿumrak, fi saṭrēn), and as majlis talk. Then, with a tutor or exchange partner, give the majlis version live and let them argue back for 10 minutes.
